rules.title: Default maximum peer count is 21
Outbound share is 15 percent with a floor of 10 outbound peers
calcOutPeers rounds (maxPeers * 15 + 50) / 100 and floors at 10
Configured maxPeers is floored at 10
Inbound slots equal maxPeers minus outPeers; without incoming, all slots are outbound
Legacy peers_max applies only when peers_in_max and peers_out_max are unset
Autoconnect tries fixed peers first and waits on fixed attempts
Autoconnect then exhausts livecache addresses before the bootcache
Autoconnect falls back to valence-ranked bootcache addresses
At most 20 simultaneous outbound connection attempts
Bootcache valence rises on success and resets to -1 on one failure
Bootcache prunes the 10 percent lowest-valence entries above 1000 entries
Per-IP inbound limit defaults to 2 and grows with inbound slots
The per-IP limit applies to public addresses only
A duplicate endpoint (same IP and port) is rejected on inbound connect
A duplicate node public key is rejected at activation
Self-connection is rejected when the local endpoint is already connected
Fixed and reserved slots bypass the inbound and outbound caps
Non-reserved slots activate only while their direction count is below its max
Inbound activation fails with inboundDisabled when no inbound slots exist
A full peer answers HTTP 503 with up to 10 redirect endpoints
An outbound connection attempt times out after 15 seconds
The session signature binds the TLS session to the node key via the finished-message hash
A missing or unverifiable session signature drops the connection
A peer on a different network identifier is rejected
A peer whose clock is more than 20 seconds off is rejected
The node public key must be a secp256k1 key
Local-IP and Remote-IP headers must agree with the observed addresses for public peers
A malformed Server-Domain header is rejected
Connect-As must include peer and the protocol version must be negotiable
The peer timer evicts large send queues, diverged and unknown outbound peers, and ping timeouts
Queries are refused once the send queue reaches 192 messages
Idle peers are deleted on every fourth one-second timer tick
The resource manager disconnects endpoints that exceed their resource limit
Endpoint gossip drops entries over 6 hops, duplicates, and invalid addresses
Oversize endpoint messages are sampled at random and acceptance is rate-limited to once per 151 seconds
Livecache entries live 30 seconds and expire once per second
A neighbor's endpoint enters the livecache only after its listening port passes a connectivity check

external.quote: IANA has assigned port 2459 for the XRP Ledger peer protocol, and you can configure which port(s) your server uses in the xrpld.cfg file. The example config file now listens for incoming peer protocol connections on port 2459 on all network interfaces. Older servers may use the previous port 51235, so you might see peers on either port.

rules.title: IANA assigned port 2459 for the peer protocol; older servers use 51235

external.quote: If you delete the server's databases, it creates a new node key pair, effectively coming online with a different identity.

rules.title: Deleting the databases creates a new node key pair and a new identity

external.quote: The key idea is to cache pongs and send only the best N pongs to a client.

rules.title: PeerFinder endpoint gossip follows the Gnutella revised ping/pong scheme: cache pongs, send only the best N

external.quote: To participate in the XRP Ledger, xrpld servers connect to arbitrary peers using the peer protocol. (All peers are treated as untrusted, unless they are clustered with the current server.)

rules.title: All peers are treated as untrusted unless they are clustered with the server
Eclipse threshold: one attacker IP offering 10 distinct ports fills all 10 default outbound slots
Partition rejoin: refilling 10 outbound slots after total honest loss takes 2 autoconnect rounds
Live-network eclipse resistance against an attacker with many distinct public IPs
